newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania Socialists jam stadium for election rally.
newsitem.headline: Albania Socialists jam stadium for election rally.

text.p: Thousands of Albanian Socialist Party supporters chanting "down with dictatorship" jammed into a soccer stadium on Tuesday, vowing to defeat President Sali Berisha in June elections.

An estimated 15,000 to 20,000 people poured into the stadium in downtown Tirana for the party's first campaign rally to hear leaders denounce Berisha, demand an end to the state of emergency and pledge to lead the party to victory on June 29.

"People will vote for the Socialist Party and the progressive opposition because they want a normal Albania for all Albanians," party chairman Fatos Nano told the enthusiastic crowd who waved banners saying "Lift the state of emergency" and "We want free elections".
"We are for a free Albania and not for the slavery of the Berisha regime," Nano said.

"There must be private capital for you and not for a handful of bandits," Nano said, in a reference to shady pyramid investment schemes which stripped thousands of Albanians of their life savings and triggered widespread riots in March.

"Altogether let's build a new Albania, based on social justice and solidarity," Nano said during the hour-rally, punctuated by shouts of "Long Live Vlore" in support of the southern port city where the riots began.
Other speakers denounced the continuation of the state of emergency enacted during the rioting and imposing a nationwide curfew from 9 p.m. to 5 a.m.
Several speakers said a free vote could not be guaranteed under curfew and at the very least polling must end at 6 p.m. to assure that Berisha operatives did not have free access to ballot boxes.
"There can be no free elections with the state of emergency and we want free elections that will assure the victory of the Socialist Party," said Pandeli Majko, the party's public affairs secretary.

Namik Dokle, the party's organisation secretary, made reference to the tens of thousands of guns looted during the rioting and said it was time to end insecurity in Albania, where gunshots are a routine part of nighttime background noise.

"We don't want our children troubled by shooting in the night, we want our mothers to feel free to take their children to school," Dokle said. "We want a democracy where everyone wins and nobody will lose."
The rally was the biggest of any party in the campaign so far and marked a beginning of the campaign by the Socialists. Berisha began campaigning two weeks ago.
The rally went off without incident.
"We've always voted Socialist but our votes were always stolen and when we went into the streets and protested we were beaten," said Valentina Ymeri, a woman in her 40s attending the rally.
"But we were not rebels, we are the true democrats," she said.

Earlier Socialist Party officials said lifting the state of emergency was a pre-requisite to holding free elections. But at the weekend, Albanian television quoted Berisha as saying it was no longer within his power to end the state of emergency, because only Parliament has authority to do so and it has been dissolved.
